title: 62 New Texas State Troopers Graduate as DPS Welcomes Its 183rd Class
excerpt: Sixty-two new Texas Highway Patrol Troopers graduated Friday in Cedar Park, completing 30 weeks of training to become the Texas Department of Public Safety's 183rd graduating class. They report to duty stations across Texas on Dec. 13.
content:
Sixty-two new Texas Highway Patrol Troopers crossed the graduation stage Friday in Cedar Park, officially joining the ranks of the Texas Department of Public Safety as its 183rd graduating class.

The graduation ceremony for Recruit Class B-2026 was held at Hill Country Bible Church, with Gov. Greg Abbott delivering the keynote address. Abbott thanked the graduates and their families, and the 31 recruit classes that have graduated during his time as governor.

“Our state is stronger because of those who carry the badge,” Abbott said, thanking the new Troopers for their commitment, bravery and willingness to serve Texans.

The road to the badge was narrow. A total of 2,368 people applied for Class B-2026. Only 90 received offers to join the class — fewer than 4 percent of applicants — and 82 met DPS standards to begin training on day one. After 30 weeks at the DPS Training Academy, with more than 1,197 hours of instruction, 62 graduated.

“For 30 weeks, Class B-2026 demonstrated the grit, determination, integrity and resolve that it takes to become Texas State Troopers,” said DPS Col. Freeman F. Martin.

The class includes 59 men and three women, ages 21 to 45. Twenty-two of the graduates are military veterans, 25 speak more than one language — including one graduate who speaks six — and four are DPS legacies.

Earlier in the week, the class completed the traditional Legacy Run, a five-mile run from DPS headquarters to the Texas State Capitol marking the end of academy training.

The newly commissioned Troopers will report to their duty stations across Texas on Dec. 13.

Sources: Texas Department of Public Safety.
